summary.text: Son of Apollo by Psamathe, daughter of Crotopus king of Argos; exposed by his mother and destroyed by the king's sheepdogs, his death brought Apollo's Vengeance upon the city.
Not Linus the Theban musician, brother of Orpheus and teacher of Heracles, whom Apollodorus places at Thebes — nor the separate 'Linus the poet' whose grave Pausanias also saw at Argos.

story.text: When Psamathe daughter of Crotopus bore Apollo a son, she exposed the infant in fear of her father. Crotopus' sheepdogs found the child and destroyed him; Apollo sent Vengeance against Argos to punish the Argives for the death.

At Argos Pausanias saw among the graves that of Linus, son of Apollo by Psamathe the daughter of Crotopus. He had already related the history of this Linus beside the grave of Coroebus at Megara, where the story equally concerns Argos.
